cap: Every prenatal test has a gestational-age window. Date the pregnancy with the crown-rump length in the first trimester, screen for aneuploidy from 10 weeks, find neural tube defects at 15 to 22 weeks, test glucose at 24 to 28 weeks, give Tdap at 27 to 36 weeks, and culture for group B strep at 36 to 37 weeks.
teach: Gestational age counts from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP). Naegele's rule adds 7 days to the LMP and subtracts 3 months, assuming a 28-day cycle; ultrasound redates the pregnancy when the two differ by more than 5 days before 9 weeks or more than 7 days from 9 to 16 weeks (more than 10, 14 and 21 days later). Preterm is before 37 weeks, early term 37 to 38 6/7, full term 39 to 40 6/7, late term 41 to 41 6/7 and post-term 42 weeks or later. TPAL counts term births, preterm births, abortions (losses before 20 weeks) and living children; a patient pregnant now who has had an ectopic pregnancy, a term birth and a stillbirth at 24 weeks, with one living child, is G4 P1111. Fundal height in centimeters matches the weeks from 20 weeks, when the fundus reaches the umbilicus. Folic acid 0.4 mg daily starts before conception and continues through the first trimester, and 4 mg daily is used after a prior neural tube defect. Anti-D immune globulin is given at 28 weeks to Rh-negative patients. MMR and varicella are live vaccines and wait until after delivery.
